candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 78-year-old man and a U.S. national. He is White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people identifying with European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries. He lives in Colorado and is married to Irene; they have no children. Their gross household income is about $262,000 a year, combining retirement income, investments, and occasional engineering consulting. He identifies as moderately conservative, valuing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while accepting that some public programs are useful. He enjoys reading, especially engineering histories, biographies, and novels.
candidates.life_course: He studied civil engineering, then spent most of his career on water and public-works projects, eventually supervising teams rather than doing fieldwork every day. He and Irene met through mutual friends and built a quiet household around work, friends, and outdoor interests. He retired from full-time work several years ago but still reviews technical plans for a few clients.
candidates.daily_life: He starts with coffee and the newspaper, then often walks a familiar nearby route with Irene. He keeps in touch with former colleagues, helps with occasional neighborhood projects, and likes having a few uncommitted days each week. He reads in the evening and trades book recommendations with Irene.
candidates.travel: He prefers scenic trips with time to stop, rather than a schedule packed with attractions. He and Irene usually travel together, by car or train, and have the time and financial flexibility for a longer trip when they plan ahead. Mountain scenery, small towns, and a comfortable place to return to at day’s end appeal to him; he likes moderate walks but does not want every day to be strenuous. On a past drive through the Southwest, they deliberately chose fewer overnight stops and spent extra time at a national park instead of trying to cover more ground. He is open to different ways of making future trips.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is measured and practical, and he likes to understand the plan before agreeing to it. He does not need every detail settled, but dislikes being hurried through a place. In conversation he may say, “Let’s leave enough time to enjoy it,” then listen carefully to Irene’s preferences before deciding.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 85-year-old man, a U.S. national, and White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category including European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries. He lives in Wyoming and is married to Ruth; they have no children. Their gross household income is approximately $224,000 per year, from retirement income, investments, and Ruth’s limited bookkeeping work for a few longstanding clients. He describes his politics as moderately conservative: tradition and personal responsibility matter to him, government should have limits, and some public programs serve a legitimate purpose. He enjoys leisure reading, especially biographies, business history, and local history.
candidates.life_course: After studying business administration, Philip joined a small commercial printing company and eventually became its owner. He and Ruth worked together through busy periods, though she kept her own professional interests. Selling the business allowed him to retire gradually instead of stopping abruptly. They chose a life without children and have maintained close friendships with former employees and neighbors.
candidates.daily_life: His mornings are often spent reading, handling household tasks, or meeting a friend for coffee. He and Ruth share meals and errands, and he stays in touch with a small circle of former colleagues. He enjoys baseball, but is equally content to follow a game at home. He prefers a familiar routine with occasional plans to look forward to.
candidates.travel: He likes domestic trips that combine a clear purpose with room to relax: a ball game, a museum, a historic district, or a visit with old friends. Ruth is his usual companion, and sometimes another couple joins them. They have enough time and resources to travel comfortably, but he tends to choose a manageable itinerary over an elaborate one. On a past trip to Chicago, he arranged the visit around a baseball game and a history museum, leaving open time for meals and wandering rather than booking something for every hour. He remembers the conversations and atmosphere as much as the sights, and has not settled on what kind of trip he would choose next.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is sociable in a low-key way and has a dry, understated humor. He likes to hear the practical details, then makes decisions without much fuss. He can be nostalgic without insisting that the past was better in every respect; a typical remark is, “We had a good time, and we didn’t have to race around to prove it.”

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 77-year-old man and a U.S. national. He is White, non-Hispanic, in the broad census-style category that includes people identifying with European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries. His home is in Montana. He is married to Marjorie, and they have no children. Their gross household income is about $238,000 annually, mainly from retirement income, investments, and occasional mediation work. He identifies as moderately conservative, with an emphasis on tradition, individual responsibility, and restrained government, while accepting some public programs. He reads for pleasure and personal interest, particularly legal history, biographies, and books about landscapes and wildlife.
candidates.life_course: Philip studied law and spent much of his career as an attorney handling workplace disputes. In later years he shifted toward mediation, which gave him more control over his schedule. Marjorie worked in nonprofit administration before retiring. They made a deliberate decision not to have children and have built long-running friendships through work, reading groups, and community activities.
candidates.daily_life: He likes a quiet start to the day, usually with a book or a long article before checking messages. A few times a week he walks outdoors with Marjorie, and he volunteers occasionally with a local literacy effort. They enjoy inviting friends over for simple meals, though he also protects stretches of unscheduled time for reading and being outside.
candidates.travel: He is drawn to trips that combine natural settings with learning something specific: birdlife, local history, or how a region has changed. Marjorie is usually his companion, and they sometimes meet friends who share an interest in walking and wildlife. With retirement and a comfortable income, they can stay longer in one place rather than rushing between destinations; he prefers a moderate pace and a quiet place to read in the evenings. On a past visit to the Oregon coast, they chose a modest base for several nights and spent their days on short walks and birdwatching, including a rainy day they treated as an excuse to read indoors. He remains open about the form of future travel.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is curious and patient, and he tends to ask questions before forming an opinion. He likes informed conversation but is not eager to dominate it. When a plan feels too crowded, he will say so plainly: “I’d rather see less and notice more.”

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 82-year-old man, a U.S. national, and White, non-Hispanic, in the broad census-style category that includes European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries. He lives in Idaho and is married to Vivian; they have no children. Their gross household income is around $281,000 a year, coming from retirement income, investments, and Vivian’s occasional interior-design consulting. Philip identifies as moderately conservative, emphasizing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while recognizing a role for some public programs. He enjoys reading for leisure, especially books on architecture, design, food, and memoir.
candidates.life_course: He trained in cabinetmaking and later built a small custom-furniture business, working closely with designers and homeowners. Vivian worked in interior design, and their professional interests often overlapped without making home life entirely about work. Philip reduced his workload over time and now takes on only occasional projects. They chose not to have children and have kept a close circle of friends from work and community life.
candidates.daily_life: He still spends some mornings in a small workshop, repairing or making a piece when he feels like it. He and Vivian share meals, go to local cultural events, and host a relaxed supper with friends now and then. He reads in the afternoon, often with a notebook nearby for sketches or ideas, and likes to keep his schedule flexible.
candidates.travel: Philip enjoys travel through the built environment: distinctive neighborhoods, old buildings, museums, markets, and food that reflects a place. Vivian is his usual companion, and they have the resources and flexibility to take a longer international trip or a shorter city break. He prefers an unhurried itinerary with comfortable lodging and time to sit down between walks; he is more interested in seeing a few places closely than collecting destinations. On a past visit to Mexico City, he and Vivian spent time looking at architecture and exploring food markets, and he chose a slower day after realizing that too many planned stops made the trip feel like work. He has no particular future trip committed to yet.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is observant and visually minded, often noticing materials, proportions, and small details that others pass by. He enjoys sharing what he knows but is happy to be surprised by someone else’s perspective. He tends to weigh options aloud, then settles on a choice without making a production of it.
